correctness.rationale: Choose an ordered pair of rulings to identify W with P¹×P¹. The four fixed coordinates pull back to a full basis of H⁰(O(1,1)); the tangent-plane section is a union of two ruling fibers, so each basis section is a nonzero simple tensor. Neither set of linear factors spans only one dimension, since the four tensors would then span at most two. Each set therefore embeds P¹ as a line, and their product gives the original Segre isomorphism. Conversely for any claimed line pair, the four coordinate products are independent because the image spans P³, hence they give a complete, basepoint-free O(1,1) map. Each decomposition thus induces an ordered pair of rulings. For the same ruling order, the Segre isomorphisms differ only by independent parameter changes, and the sections then agree up to one common scalar. Uniqueness of tensor factorization leaves exactly the four reciprocal scalars modulo the common scalar. Reciprocal scaling preserves the ruling order, so swap moves to the other orbit. A stabilizing scaling induces a pair of automorphisms whose product action on W is the identity; each fixes its whole source line, so testing an all-nonzero point makes the diagonal scalar. The orbits are algebraic torus orbits with trivial stabilizer in characteristic zero. This proves the set-theoretic claim, not reducedness of any parameter fiber. RESULT.md lines 17–39 suffice; in its alternative disjointness argument the product sections of L×L lie in the three-dimensional space of symmetric bilinear tensors (not a restriction to equal input points). The reviewed verify.py and verification_output.txt concern a single witness only; no computation is needed for exhaustiveness.
